Shehla Faizi

Green candidate for Comptroller of Public Accounts, Texas · Challenger

Not confirmed in sources reviewed

Shehla Faizi is the Green Party nominee for Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts in the November 3, 2026 general election. She was nominated at the Green Party convention held April 11, 2026. She is running against Don Huffines (R), Sarah Eckhardt (D) and V. Alonzo Echavarria-Garza (L).

Where Faizi stands

School vouchers (Education Freedom Accounts)
Opposes the Texas school voucher program. Cites data showing that most applicants already attended private schools and asks why tax dollars are going into private hands.
Data centers
Pledges no tax breaks for data centers. Calls for more transparency from the comptroller's office on data center construction, saying there is no solid data on the job benefits of AI data centers.
State contracting and corruption
Pledges unbiased state contracts. Says she would stop enforcing the state anti-boycott law that requires state contractors to pledge in writing not to take part in the BDS movement against Israel, and supports repealing anti-BDS laws.
Role and independence of the office
Says the comptroller should answer to the people, not party bosses or big donors. Says she accepts no billionaire, PAC or lobbyist money, and calls money in politics the biggest challenge facing Texas.
Transparency of state spending
Proposes billboards about the state budget, modeled on TxDOT's road-safety billboards. Calls for all content on the comptroller's website to be available in Spanish.
State investments in foreign bonds
Pledges that no taxpayer dollars will go to foreign bonds. Says Texas should divest from Israeli bonds and redirect its $280 million investment to Texas.
Immigration enforcement funding
Campaign pledge: 'Texas Sheriffs for Texans - not ICE.'
